blocks.text: A valid two-pointer method explains what candidate region or output boundary remains and why a particular move cannot discard a needed state. Alternating movement may happen to terminate while still skipping valid candidates. A single loop may bound operation count, but it does not prove the answer contract. The diagnostic boundary is whether movement is semantically licensed by the problem structure.

blocks.text: The invariant is that all positions outside the current boundaries have already been verified as matching mirror pairs. When the current endpoints match, advancing both pointers preserves that invariant and reduces the unresolved region. If they differ, the decision is complete immediately. Moving both happens to be valid here because both endpoints are jointly discharged, not because moving both is a universal two-pointer rule.

blocks.text: In sorted pair search, exactly one boundary usually moves after a mismatch. In palindrome comparison, both verified endpoints can move together. In stable compaction, read advances every step while write advances only for accepted values. Treating movement as a syntactic recipe loses the correctness boundary that defines each variant.

blocks.text: Two-pointer recognition is mechanism-based. Opposite ends can shrink an ordered candidate region, read/write pointers can separate consumed input from produced output, and partition pointers can delimit classified and unclassified regions. Exhaustive pair enumeration has no monotonic elimination, while independent prefix and suffix passes do not form one coordinated state. The family includes multiple variants, but each needs a shared invariant that explains movement.

Omitting this incorrectly narrows two pointers to opposite ends; same-direction read/write is a legal variant.

blocks.text: The left scan skips values already on the correct side, and the right scan does the analogous work for failing values. When both stop on violations, swapping repairs two positions and grows the classified regions. This is a boundary-maintenance problem, not full sorting. Stability is a separate transfer boundary: an opposite-ends swap partition does not preserve within-group order.

blocks.text: Before each read step, positions before write contain exactly the accepted values seen so far in original order. The read pointer advances for every input value, while write advances only when the current value is kept. That conditional relationship is a two-pointer invariant even though both pointers move in the same direction. Sorting is neither required nor harmless when stability is part of the output contract.

blocks.text: With a nondecreasing array, a sum below the target can only be increased by advancing the left boundary, while a sum above the target can only be decreased by retreating the right boundary. That relationship coordinates the pointers and shrinks one candidate region. Merely having two indices says nothing about legal movement, and sorted input alone does not prescribe binary search. The pattern transfers when boundary comparisons support a one-direction elimination rule; it does not transfer to arbitrary pair conditions.

messages.text: Sortedness enables several strategies. Binary search is appropriate only when a legal half-discard rule matches the query; here the pair relation supports coordinated extremes instead.

blocks.text: In an unsorted array, the values at the physical ends are not the smallest and largest remaining candidates, so moving either pointer after a mismatch can discard a valid solution. A hash lookup can preserve original indices without mutation under the allowed memory budget. Returning indices does not categorically forbid sorting-based methods, but sorting would require a decorated copy or mutation, both excluded here. The decisive boundary is legal elimination, not the surface phrase ‘pair sum.’

messages.text: Memory availability broadens the strategy set; it does not prohibit pointer methods. It makes a hash-based alternative feasible here.
Indices can be preserved by sorting value-index pairs when copying or mutation is permitted. The present blocker is the combination of unsorted input and the no-sort constraints.
Pair-sum on sorted input is a canonical opposite-ends use case. The missing ordered relation, not the objective itself, blocks it.
